comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C79-C82. Both evaluations support that GdnHCl experiments demonstrate the requirement for both Hsp104 localization and activity for curing. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic interpretation while peer reviewers acknowledge the convincing demonstration of activity-dependent asymmetric retention.

Perfect agreement on claims C98-C103. Both evaluations support the temporal analysis showing that substrate resolution kinetics relative to cell division timing determines Hsp104 retention and curing efficiency. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the novel spatiotemporal mechanism.

Significant disagreement on claims C56-C64 regarding Hsp104 engagement with heat-induced aggregates. OpenEval finds the co-immunocapture and localization data provide strong support, while peer reviewers express concern about the correlative nature of evidence and request direct demonstration of interaction (e.g., co-immunoprecipitation, aggregate isolation).

Disagreement on claims C83-C96 regarding cell-cycle stage dependence. OpenEval finds the synchronization experiments provide strong support for cell-cycle dependency, while peer reviewer 1 expresses concern about nocodazole confounding effects and suggests removing or moving this section to supplement, questioning whether cell cycle dependency is sufficiently established.

Strong agreement on claims C65-C78. Both evaluations support that Hsp104 asymmetric retention correlates with and is required for curing. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as novel and exciting, with the spatiotemporal mechanism being convincingly demonstrated through BNI1 disruption and single-cell analysis.

Agreement on claims C35-C38, C133-C137. Both evaluations support that differential responses of [PSI+]Strong and [PSI+]Weak demonstrate that amplification dynamics rather than stability determine clearance susceptibility. Peer reviewers acknowledge the clever manipulation enabling strong [PSI+] curing as a key insight.

Agreement on claims C4, C25, C29-C31, C34. Both evaluations support the experimental demonstration of temperature-specific effects on [PSI+]Weak curing and Hsp104-dependent amyloid disassembly. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the convincing demonstration of heat-induced aggregate retention of Hsp104 and Sup35 disaggregation.

Partial overlap on claims C32-C33. Both evaluations support Hsp104 involvement in amyloid disassembly based on GdnHCl curing and heterozygous deletion experiments. Peer reviewer 2 notes this establishes necessity but not sufficiency, while OpenEval considers the evidence strong for Hsp104 dependence.

Disagreement on claims C43-C47 regarding comparison between thermal stress and Hsp104 overexpression. OpenEval finds the data provide strong evidence for distinct mechanisms, while peer reviewer 2 notes overexpression data is 'currently not shown' and requests demonstration that overexpression to the same level achieved through asymmetric retention suffices to induce curing.

Disagreement on claims C48-C53 regarding aggregate quantification. OpenEval finds the differential centrifugation and immunoblotting data support temperature-dependent aggregate accumulation, while peer reviewer 2 raises methodological concerns about insufficient protocol description and requests more rigorous quantification using alternative procedures like sucrose-density gradients.

Agreement on claims C106-C108, C130. Both evaluations support the major conclusions about multiple cell-based factors determining proteostasis capacity. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize the concept that temporary sequestration of proteostasis factors can be beneficial as novel and exciting, and accept the spatiotemporal framework as a significant contribution.

Partial agreement on claims C109-C115 regarding broader relevance. OpenEval finds the background context well-supported by citations, while peer reviewers 2 and 3 express uncertainty about extrapolation to metazoans and request clarification on whether concepts are yeast-specific or broadly applicable, particularly regarding Hsp110 speculation.

Agreement on claims C116-C118 regarding aggregate structures. Both evaluations support the existence of spatially restricted aggregates with associated chaperones. Peer reviewer 2 requests better integration of Q-bodies, iPOD, JUNQ, and aggresome literature into the discussion but does not dispute the underlying concepts.

Agreement on claims C67-C68 regarding Ssa1 and Sis1 localization. Both evaluations support this observation as evidence for specificity of Hsp104 asymmetric retention. Peer reviewer 2 requests examination of other Hsp70/Hsp40 isoforms but does not challenge the presented localization data.

Minimal overlap on claim C132. Both evaluations support conclusions about proteostasis capacity being finely tuned, with peer reviewers accepting this as part of the overall conceptual framework without specific challenge.

Minimal overlap on claim C119. Both evaluations support this conclusion, with OpenEval finding it well-supported by collective evidence and peer reviewers accepting it as part of the novel spatiotemporal mechanism framework.

OpenEval finds claims C1-C3, C7-C11 (established background on proteostasis networks and amyloid biology) well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these specific background claims.

OpenEval finds claims C12-C22, C27-C28 (background on [PSI+] variants and temperature sensitivity) well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval finds claims C128-C129, C140-C141 (conclusions and speculations about therapeutic implications) appropriately supported and distinguished from established findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative conclusions.
